n: William W. Phelps, a newspaper editor and printer, had come to Kirtland to learn God’s will for him. The Lord calls him and promises forgiveness and the Holy Ghost if he is baptized with pure motives.

f.g: William Wines Phelps (1792–1872), later the Church’s printer and author of many hymns, including “The Spirit of God.”

f.w: an eye single to my glory

n: After baptism, Joseph Smith will ordain him an elder to preach repentance and baptism in Jesus Christ’s name.

f.w: baptism in the name of Jesus Christ

n: He will have power to confer the Holy Ghost on those who are contrite.

f.w: you shall have power to give the Holy Spirit

n: He will help Oliver Cowdery with printing and with selecting and writing schoolbooks, so even children may be taught in ways pleasing to God. This is one of the earliest scriptural mandates for Church education.

f.g: Phelps later published the Church’s first newspaper and the Book of Commandments in Missouri.

n: For this purpose he will travel to Missouri with Joseph and Sidney and be “planted” in the land of inheritance.
Joseph Coe is also to go with them. More instructions will come later.

f.g: An early convert from New York who settled in Kirtland.
